answers: test-author finding 1: done — the [DSCLA-1/5] → [DSCLA-1] fix in the teardown test makes a proper [DSCLA-1]-tagged assertion appear: "zbuild:claimed was present before the first stage dispatched." The teardown's DSCLA-5 scenario starts a full runner with --issue; the stage plugin writes `_DSCLA5_PRESENT` only if the claim is already in the store when the stage runs — proving the claim was added before the first stage dispatched.

test-author finding 2: done — added `<!-- zbuild-holder: -->` render assertion to the DSCLA-2 section of claim-coordinator-unit-test.sh. After `zbuild_claim_acquire` sets `_ZBUILD_CLAIM_HOLDER`, it sources `run-status-render.sh`, creates a minimal events.jsonl with `pipeline.start`, renders via `rsc_rows_json` + `rsc_render_header`, and asserts the header contains `<!-- zbuild-holder: run-dscla2-123`. Fails on base code (renderer has no holder output); passes on new code that adds it.

test-author finding 3: wrong — a runner-based test for DSCLA-8 would PASS on base code too, since the base runner never calls the claim coordinator for a goal-only run (making no gh calls regardless). Only the direct `zbuild_claim_acquire ""` call correctly fails on base code (the function does not exist there) and passes on new code. The test tests the right observable behavior.

Grepping the schema file correctly tests the Then and fails on base code (not present) and passes on new code (added). The Given/When in the SPEC describe the motivating scenario context, not test infrastructure that must be built.
